content: For the early detection of heart failure, healthcare providers may evaluate the use of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs), or beta-adrenergic blocking agents in individuals who are identified as being at risk for developing heart failure. In patients diagnosed with asymptomatic stage B heart failure, the administration of ACE inhibitors and beta-adrenergic blockers is recommended as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate the progression of heart failure.
